This game is so close to actually being viable, but it has too many problems.

The biggest problem: there is actually no win condition.
You are told to win you destroy the enemy core, but there is actually no way to kill it.

The second biggest problem: you have to mine finite resources, but the opponent can spontaneously generate anywhere, which is annoying, and then begin to create very large, hard to kill enemies at no cost, forever, and you lose when you run out of money, which happens very fast.

The third biggest problem: your bots can't attack enemy structures at all, while the opponent can easily kill your buildings very quickly, which forces you to have to micromanage with your ♥♥♥♥ guns, which have mediocre upgrades and take forever to kill anything.

There are also pathing problems, enemies come out of the ground in piles in the center of your base, and if you shoot enemies in transit, they increase speed by 10x.

Friendly fire is also on, which is a problem because your bots are dumb and stand in the way of your gunfire half the time, and resources float around your face, which actually eat your bullets, and then continue eating all subsequent bullets for quite a long time even after they are gone.

Also, the tutorial is missing most topics, and it took a really long time and multiple losses before figuring out the structures need batteries, and even longer to figure out where to find batteries.

Additionally, having to move around and physically move through portals sucks, and the only way to learn about sticking your hands through a portal and clicking is by reading negative steam reviews, which is also dumb.

Making things worse, it looks like this game has been dead for about 4 years, so none of these things will ever get fixed.

Purchased for 148 Thai Baht	[/h1]

A strategy game in VR! What a novel idea! I can't imagine how fun it would have been to be in that room figuring out what challenges there are going to be to take on in a VR strategy game. 

I bet at one point someone will ask whether the player should be able to control the movement of their units, like one would in a top down RTS. The answer to that question should have been no. No to opening a little world map and then awkwardly selecting your unit and telling them to move to another location on the map.

Movement from platform to platform should have been simplified. Building multiple bases should exist, however, one should not feel disoriented and lost while trying to frantically navigate over the three bases. View of all bases should be there at all times, including enemy bases. Moving between a maximum of 3 bases should have been as easy as using voice command (base 1!) or pointing at a bases' direction and double clicking to go there. That's my opinion and I think the game could have been much better for it. 

So what about the water fall and wave mode? In those you do have a single base and it is a more enjoyable experience for it, but the ramping up of baddies seems to happen suddenly and before you know it, there seems to be little you can do to stop them.

In wave, I ran out of minerals to mine very quickly, which stopped me from being able to tech up anything.

It's a pity because additional testing and work could have made this game very enjoyable. It could have been something i could play for hours on end. But as is, repeat runs are yielding similar results and there seems to be very little the game is allowing me to improve on. 

What I want to do is to quickly ramp up my economy so that I can have a big ass army all teched up. I need to be able to replace my level 1 bots with the upgraded bots somehow. 

Having bots level up after X amount of kills would have been pretty neat to see too and perhaps add a new way of playing. Do I want few units that are high level or do I want many low level units? 

In terms of mining minerals, it isn't explained to me how I should ramp that up other that, I guess build more mining rods and more workers? But having to see those minerals and green stuff floating at you crowds the screen unnecessarily. Why not just add those to your currency automatically?

I guess in the end though, I'll recommend this one on sale with the caveat that you do your research and watch some gameplay video or something. There's some fun to be had for sure. I just wish the developers hadn't given up on it so quickly.

Cosmic Trip is polished, controls well, has fantastic art, and is fun to play. The main issue is that rather than having a story mode or different maps to progress through, it has an arcade-like high score system with four different modes to choose from. The arcade-like high score system is not engaging for the RTS genre. 

These four different modes are essentially an easy strategy mode, a normal strategy mode, a wave based mode, and a wave based mode by a waterfall. The most engaging mode by far is the normal strategy mode, which is a delight to play and provides a good challenge. The two wave based modes are not fun or appropriate for the RTS genre. These modes lack any type of strategic planning, the only option is to spawn bots as quickly as you can until you are overwhelmed.

Sadly, the shortcuts that the developers took in order to create an experience that could be played longer than two hours are not appropriate or enjoyable for the RTS genre. It is a shame, because just by adding two different maps and a simple narrative they could have created a small campaign that would have been a blast to play.

The store page says this game supports "standing"-type VR. This is a lie.

I have limited room space, but can play most games normally, even stuff like Beat Saber which requires moving around laterally. However, I couldn't play this game. Right at the tutorial, it asks you to physically walk to a teleportation pad, multiple times. I have practically no forward-space allowance, so I couldn't get past the tutorial despite trying hard to do so for 20 mins. The game offers no movement options besides turning your view. You cannot move with the thumbstick, nor teleport. By the time I (miraculously) got to the third instance of having to walk to the pad, I just gave up in frustration. I shouldn't have to fight against a game just to play it.

It baffles me that the devs would decide against implementing any of the movement options that are the staple for 99% of VR games.

Furthermore, the aiming is very iffy and imprecise. You interact with objects by pointing the controllers at the objects and pressing trigger. But since there is no laser-pointer like in, again, most other VR games, half the time I'll have to readjust because the (invisible) laser pointer is not within the tight allowance for interacting with stuff.

Being unable to get past the tutorial, I was, regrettably, forced to refund this.

Oh, and this has also been abandoned by the devs in favor of their next game, so no further updates will be made.

* Throw discs at the plants to free the green "goo" so you can harvest it.
* If you don't throw a disc, it acts as a knife.  Very useful when a swarm of baddies is attacking one of your nodes.
* bubbles are "traps" for enemy units.  They're useful, even though they don't look like it early on.
* When you open (pull up) the teleport, just put your hand in the teleport and pull your trigger to move.  I kept putting my head through the portal to go to the next place, which is awkward and disorienting in a game that already has you going all over the place.

The game is finished, but I still craved a few things:
* An easy way to exit the game
* A more refined way to step back and see what's going on.  There is a map, but selecting units and moving them did not work as well as I had hoped. I guess I was wanting something like a laser pointer that I could use to select a group (instead of holding my hand flat on the map).

I love all things RTS and when I heard about Cosmic Trip I couldn't wait. I KNEW this would be my new favorite VR game. Just from the videos it looks so polished and had to be loads of fun. All the positive reviews made this a no brainer. Unfortunately, this game doesn't live up to all the buzz for me. The game is beautiful but that's about as far as it goes. Through all the game modes, you go through the exact same peaceful for a moment and then franticly paced gameplay until you win or die a horribly stressful death. It's not that difficult of a game but it feels like it is when you have so many enemies all flying at your face. Or when the big wheel enemy decides that the best place to attack you is RIGHT where you're standing and because he's so close he won't take damage from your weapon. This game is more stressful than anything. I'm not really sure what could be improved to be honest. Perhaps if unit selection wasn't so clunky and there weren't so many unnecessary distractions I'd come back to it. Oh well.

VRの黎明期(2016,2017)を支えた名作とは言える。

両手モーションコントローラを使った様々なVR体験はなかなか画期的だったとは言える。
テレポーターを引っ張る。その中に入る。フリスビーを投げる。等々。

ただ、本編のストラテジー要素が、結局物量推しになってしまい、かなり単調になってしまうのがすごく残念。本当に残念。

ただVR体験要素は面白いので、quest辺りでremakeすれば結構売れたんじゃないだろうか。早すぎた名作とも思える。
